messages:
Diego Ramos: Heads up — moving from NY to SF in mid-Jan and I need to switch from our national PPO to the CA HMO. Also newborn arriving next month; want to add baby to medical and dental at the same time. What do I need and timeline for plan change + dependent add?
Maya Singh: congrats Diego! :tada: moving states + newborn are QLEs. For plan network change we need proof of CA residence (lease or utility) and for newborn you'll need birth cert or hospital record. Ideally submit both within 30 days of the move / birth.
Ben Chu: short practical notes:
```
- If you want HMO effective 1st of month, enroll/change must be completed before the last payroll cut-off of previous month.
- Newborn coverage can be effective on date of birth if submitted within 30 days.
- If both events overlap (birth then move) pick which effective dates you prefer on the form; we can coordinate retro adjustments where allowed.
```
Diego Ramos: can I temporarily keep my NY PCP for baby until I move? worried about continuity of care for 2 weeks.
Kelsey O'Neil: most HMOs require providers in-network; we can request an exception for a short overlap but it's not guaranteed. Option: enroll baby on NY PPO at birth and then submit a QLE to move baby to CA HMO when you establish CA residence — that's two actions but keeps continuity. Note this might affect payroll deductions in two cycles.
Diego Ramos: ok, what's the process for doing two-step: add newborn on PPO now, then move baby to HMO later? any special forms?
Maya Singh: upload birth record to the benefits portal under "Add dependent - newborn". To later move plans, submit "Change plan - midyear move" with CA residency proof. When you do the second submission, include a note "move of dependent from PPO to HMO" and we'll coordinate billing.
Ben Chu: FYI payroll implication: if you add dependent mid-pay-period we may not prorate premium until next cycle. If you request retroactive premium adjustment for the baby (to be effective birth date) include bank/hospital receipts — payroll will review.
Payroll Bot: created ticket PAY-3342 for Diego Ramos; next payroll deadline for retro requests: 2025-01-05 17:00 PST.
Diego Ramos: perfect. I'll add baby to PPO after birth and upload docs. Also moving lease isn't signed yet — will that block the CA HMO enrollment later?
Maya Singh: not necessarily. If lease isn't signed yet, you can provide a signed intent to lease + move confirmation (flight, moving contract) and we can provisionally accept. But final proof must follow when available.
Kelsey O'Neil: quick tip — if you want single-step simplicity, wait to enroll baby until after you move and enroll both on CA HMO on the baby's birth date, but that risks missing 30-day newborn window if timing is tight. Choose whichever minimizes gaps.
Diego Ramos: thanks team — I'll upload birth cert first and ping when I have lease. Appreciate the options.
